questions.question: The stress on a joint is minimal and its capsule is most lax in the:
questions.explanation: In the loose-packed position the joint surfaces are least congruent and the capsule is slack, so joint play is maximal.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The joint surfaces are maximally congruent and the capsule and ligaments taut in the:
questions.explanation: In the close-packed position, the joint is locked and has no joint play.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the spinal facet joints is:
questions.explanation: The facet joints are close-packed in extension and loose-packed midway between flexion and extension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the spinal facet joints is:
questions.explanation: Facet joints lock in full extension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed (resting) position of the glenohumeral joint is:

options.A: 55 degrees adduction and 30 degrees horizontal abduction
options.C: 55 degrees abduction and 30 degrees horizontal adduction

questions.explanation: The GH resting position is about 55 degrees of abduction with 30 degrees of horizontal adduction (scapular plane).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the glenohumeral joint is:
questions.explanation: The shoulder capsule is maximally taut in full abduction with lateral rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the acromioclavicular joint is:
questions.explanation: The AC joint is close-packed with the arm at 90 degrees of abduction; the SC joint is close-packed in maximum shoulder elevation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the sternoclavicular joint is:
questions.explanation: The SC joint is locked in full elevation of the shoulder girdle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the ulnohumeral joint is:

options.B: 70 degrees of flexion with 10 degrees of supination
options.C: 90 degrees of flexion with 5 degrees of supination

questions.explanation: The ulnohumeral joint is open-packed in 70 degrees of flexion and 10 degrees of supination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the humeroulnar joint is:
questions.explanation: The ulnohumeral joint is close-packed in extension; the radiohumeral joint in 90 degrees of flexion and 5 degrees of supination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the radiohumeral joint is:

options.A: 90 degrees elbow flexion and 5 degrees supination

questions.explanation: The radial head is close-packed at 90 degrees of elbow flexion with 5 degrees of forearm supination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the proximal radioulnar joint is:

options.A: 70 degrees of flexion with 35 degrees of supination

questions.explanation: The proximal radioulnar joint is open-packed at 70 degrees of elbow flexion and 35 degrees of supination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the proximal and distal radioulnar joints is:
questions.explanation: Both radioulnar joints are close-packed at 5 degrees of supination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the distal radioulnar joint is:
questions.explanation: The distal radioulnar joint is open-packed at 10 degrees of supination.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the wrist joint is:
questions.explanation: The radiocarpal joint is locked in full extension with radial deviation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the wrist joint is:
questions.explanation: The wrist is open-packed in a neutral position with slight ulnar deviation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb is:
questions.explanation: The thumb CMC joint is open-packed midway between its two ranges of motion and close-packed in full opposition.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the metacarpophalangeal joints of the fingers is:
questions.explanation: The finger MCP joints are locked in full flexion, whereas the IP joints are locked in full extension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the interphalangeal joints of the fingers is:
questions.explanation: IP joints lock in full extension and rest in slight flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the hip joint is:

options.A: 30 degrees flexion, 30 degrees abduction and slight lateral rotation
options.B: 30 degrees flexion, 30 degrees adduction and slight medial rotation

questions.explanation: The hip is open-packed at 30 degrees of flexion and abduction with slight lateral rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The open-packed position of the knee joint is:
questions.explanation: The knee is loose-packed at about 25 degrees of flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The loose-packed position of the ankle joint is:

options.B: 10 degrees plantar flexion, midway between inversion and eversion

questions.explanation: The talocrural joint is open-packed at about 10 degrees of plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The close-packed position of the midtarsal, tarsometatarsal and subtalar joints is:
questions.explanation: These foot joints lock in supination, which makes the foot a rigid lever for push-off.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the glenohumeral joint is:

options.B: Medial rotation more limited than lateral rotation
options.C: Lateral rotation more limited than abduction, abduction more than medial rotation

questions.explanation: Cyriax capsular pattern of the shoulder: lateral rotation > abduction > medial rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the wrist is:
questions.explanation: In the wrist, both flexion and extension are limited equally.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the knee is:
questions.explanation: The knee capsular pattern is limitation of flexion greater than extension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the ankle (talocrural) joint is:

options.A: Plantar flexion more limited than dorsiflexion
options.D: Dorsiflexion more limited than plantar flexion

questions.explanation: At the talocrural joint the capsular pattern is plantar flexion greater than dorsiflexion limitation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of shoulder flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Shoulder flexion and abduction each reach about 180 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of shoulder extension is about:
questions.explanation: Shoulder extension is about 60 degrees (AAOS 45-60).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of shoulder medial (internal) rotation is about:
questions.explanation: Shoulder medial rotation is about 70 degrees; lateral rotation about 90 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of shoulder lateral (external) rotation is about:
questions.explanation: Lateral rotation of the shoulder is about 90 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of forearm pronation or supination is about:
questions.explanation: Each of pronation and supination is about 80-90 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of wrist flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Wrist flexion is about 80 degrees and extension about 70 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of wrist extension is about:
questions.explanation: Wrist extension is about 70 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of wrist radial deviation is about:
questions.explanation: Radial deviation is about 20 degrees and ulnar deviation about 30 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of wrist ulnar deviation is about:
questions.explanation: Ulnar deviation (about 30 degrees) exceeds radial deviation because the radial styloid projects further.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thumb CMC abduction is about:
questions.explanation: Thumb CMC abduction is about 70 degrees (palmar abduction).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thumb CMC extension is about:
questions.explanation: Thumb CMC extension is about 20 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thumb metacarpophalangeal flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Thumb MCP flexion is about 50 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thumb interphalangeal flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Thumb IP flexion is about 80 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of MCP flexion in the 2nd to 5th digits is about:
questions.explanation: Finger MCP flexion is about 90 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of MCP hyperextension of the 2nd to 5th digits is about:
questions.explanation: MCP hyperextension of the fingers is about 45 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of PIP flexion of the fingers is about:
questions.explanation: PIP flexion is about 100 degrees and DIP flexion about 90 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of hip flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Hip flexion with the knee bent is about 120 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of hip extension and adduction is about:
questions.explanation: Hip extension and adduction are each about 30 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of hip abduction is about:
questions.explanation: Hip abduction is about 45 degrees; medial and lateral rotation about 45 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of ankle plantar flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Ankle plantar flexion is about 50 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of foot inversion is about:
questions.explanation: Inversion is about 35 degrees and eversion about 15 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of foot eversion is about:
questions.explanation: Eversion is about 15 degrees, much less than inversion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of cervical flexion, extension and lateral flexion (each) is about:
questions.explanation: Each of cervical flexion, extension and lateral flexion is about 45 degrees; rotation is about 80 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thoracolumbar flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Thoracolumbar flexion is about 80 degrees, extension about 25 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thoracolumbar extension is about:
questions.explanation: Thoracolumbar extension is about 25 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thoracolumbar lateral flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Thoracolumbar lateral flexion is about 35 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal range of thoracolumbar rotation is about:
questions.explanation: Thoracolumbar rotation is about 45 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Acute joint inflammation (e.g. synovitis or bursitis) typically presents with which end feel?
questions.explanation: An empty end feel means movement is stopped by pain before any tissue resistance is felt, as in acute inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Capsular tightness presents with which end feel?
questions.explanation: Capsular tightness gives a firm, leathery end feel with a stretch that cannot be pushed through.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An osteophyte limiting joint motion produces which end feel?
questions.explanation: Bony contact (osteophyte, fracture, bony block) gives an abrupt hard end feel.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Oedema around a joint typically produces which end feel?
questions.explanation: Soft-tissue swelling gives a soft, boggy end feel.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A ligament tear with instability would typically present with which end feel?
questions.explanation: With a complete ligament rupture there is no restraining tissue, so movement is limited only by pain or apprehension (empty).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Muscle spasm presents with which end feel?
questions.explanation: Muscle guarding gives a sudden, rubbery resistance that stops movement short of the normal range.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A loose body within a joint produces which end feel?
questions.explanation: Intra-articular displacement (loose body, meniscal block) gives a springy rebound at a block short of the normal range.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A fracture limiting joint motion produces which end feel?
questions.explanation: Bone-to-bone contact stops motion abruptly.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the posterior part of the head is supplied by which spinal level?
questions.explanation: The C2 dermatome covers the occiput and posterior scalp; C3 covers the posterolateral neck.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the acromioclavicular joint is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: The AC joint area (tip of shoulder) is C4.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the lateral aspect of the upper arm is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: The C5 dermatome covers the lateral upper arm (regimental badge area is axillary nerve).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the lateral forearm and thumb is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: C6 supplies the thumb and lateral forearm.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The palmar surface of the distal phalanx of the middle finger is the key sensory area of:
questions.explanation: C7 is tested over the middle finger.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the medial border of the hand and the little finger is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: C8 supplies the little finger and ulnar border of the hand.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the medial forearm is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: T1 is tested over the medial forearm (medial epicondyle area).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the anterior thigh (upper) is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: L2 covers the upper anterior thigh; L3 the lower anterior thigh.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The key sensory area for the L3 dermatome is the:

options.C: Anterior thigh (lower part) and area above the knee

questions.explanation: L3 supplies the anterior thigh down toward the knee.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the medial malleolus and the patella region is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: L4 supplies the medial leg and medial malleolus, with L3-L4 over the knee.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the dorsum of the foot and the fibular head region is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: The L5 dermatome covers the dorsum of the foot and lateral leg.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the lateral border and sole of the foot is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: S1 supplies the lateral foot and sole.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the medial surface of the posterior thigh is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: S2 covers the posterior thigh and popliteal fossa.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Sensation over the perianal region is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: Saddle (perianal) sensation is S3-S5.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted shoulder elevation (shrugging) tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Trapezius and levator scapulae (spinal accessory and C3-C4) give the C2-C4 myotome.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted shoulder abduction tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Deltoid and supraspinatus are tested for C5.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted elbow flexion tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Biceps and brachialis represent C5-C6.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted wrist extension tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: The extensor carpi radialis muscles represent C6.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted elbow extension tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Triceps represents C7.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted wrist flexion tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Wrist flexors (FCR and FCU) represent C7.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted thumb extension tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Extensor pollicis longus and brevis represent C8.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted finger adduction/abduction tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: The hand intrinsic muscles represent T1.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted hip flexion tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Iliopsoas represents L1-L2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted knee extension tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Quadriceps represents L3-L4.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted ankle dorsiflexion tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Tibialis anterior represents mainly L4.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted great toe extension tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Extensor hallucis longus is the key L5 muscle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Resisted ankle plantar flexion tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Gastrocnemius and soleus represent S1-S2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade 3 of accessory joint motion means:
questions.explanation: Grade 3 is normal; grades 0-2 are hypomobility, 4-5 hypermobility, 6 unstable.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade 0 of accessory joint motion means:
questions.explanation: Grade 0 is no detectable motion (ankylosis).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade 1 of accessory joint motion means:
questions.explanation: Grade 1 is considerable hypomobility (a little motion present).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade 2 of accessory joint motion means:
questions.explanation: Grade 2 is slight hypomobility.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade 4 of accessory joint motion means:
questions.explanation: Grade 4 is slight hypermobility.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade 5 of accessory joint motion means:
questions.explanation: Grade 5 is considerable hypermobility.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade 6 of accessory joint motion means:
questions.explanation: Grade 6 is an unstable joint.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In facet joint dysfunction the pain is typically aggravated by:
questions.explanation: Extension and rotation compress the facet joints and aggravate facet pain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In lumbar spinal canal stenosis the pain is aggravated by:
questions.explanation: Extension narrows the canal; flexion opens it and relieves neurogenic claudication.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In lumbar spinal canal stenosis the pain is relieved by:
questions.explanation: Forward flexion enlarges the canal and relieves symptoms.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, a palpable or visible contraction with no joint movement is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 1 is a flicker of contraction without movement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, initiating movement but not completing the range in a gravity-eliminated position is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 2- is partial range in the gravity-eliminated plane.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, completing the full range in a gravity-eliminated plane is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 2 = complete range with gravity eliminated.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, initiating movement against gravity (less than half the range) is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 2+ is initiation of movement against gravity through less than half the range.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, completing the full range against gravity without added resistance is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 3 is full range against gravity alone.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, completing the full range against gravity with minimal resistance is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 3+ is full range against gravity with slight resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, full range against gravity with moderate resistance is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 4 = moderate resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On manual muscle testing, full range against gravity with maximal resistance is graded:
questions.explanation: Grade 5 = full range against maximal resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Speed's test is a provocative test for:
questions.explanation: Resisted shoulder flexion with the forearm supinated and elbow extended reproduces pain in the bicipital groove.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Neer impingement test the examiner passively:

options.A: Loads the arm downward at the side
options.B: Pulls the arm into horizontal adduction
options.C: Flexes the internally rotated arm overhead
options.D: Abducts the arm with lateral rotation

questions.explanation: Neer test: passive forward flexion with internal rotation compresses the supraspinatus against the acromion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The drop arm test is positive in:
questions.explanation: The patient cannot lower the abducted arm smoothly; it drops suddenly with a large rotator cuff tear.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The AC shear test is positive when:

options.A: Pain is reproduced when the acromioclavicular joint is compressed
options.B: Biceps tendon pops out of the groove

questions.explanation: The AC shear test compresses the AC joint by squeezing the clavicle and acromion together.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Upper limb tension test 2 (ULTT2) preferentially stresses the:

options.C: Median nerve (plus axillary and musculocutaneous nerves)

questions.explanation: ULTT1 and ULTT2a bias the median nerve; ULTT2b the radial nerve; ULTT3 the ulnar nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Upper limb tension test 3 (ULTT3) preferentially tests the:
questions.explanation: ULTT3 (shoulder depression and abduction with elbow flexion, wrist extension, ulnar deviation) biases the ulnar nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Adson's test the radial pulse is monitored while the patient rotates the head toward the involved side and extends it with deep inspiration; loss of pulse suggests:
questions.explanation: Adson's test assesses compression of the subclavian artery and brachial plexus between the scalenes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Wright's hyperabduction test, in which the shoulder is abducted and externally rotated until the radial pulse is lost, assesses:
questions.explanation: Hyperabduction compresses the neurovascular bundle beneath the coracoid and pectoralis minor.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Roos (EAST/hands-up) test is used to assess:
questions.explanation: In the Roos test the arms are held at 90 degrees abduction and external rotation while the hands open and close for 3 minutes; reproduction of symptoms is positive.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pushing the shoulders down and back (military brace position) with loss of radial pulse tests for:
questions.explanation: The Eden/costoclavicular manoeuvre narrows the space between the clavicle and first rib.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Cozen's test is a provocative test for:
questions.explanation: Resisted wrist extension with a clenched fist reproduces pain over the lateral epicondyle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pain over the medial epicondyle when the forearm is passively supinated with the elbow and wrist extended indicates:
questions.explanation: This is the passive test for medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Mill's test is positive in:
questions.explanation: Mill's test passively pronates the forearm with wrist flexion and elbow extension to stretch the common extensor origin.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Finkelstein's test is positive in:
questions.explanation: The thumb is held in the fist and the wrist is passively ulnar deviated, reproducing pain over the first dorsal compartment.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Froment's sign (paper test), the patient flexes the thumb interphalangeal joint instead of adducting the thumb to hold the paper, which indicates:
questions.explanation: Flexor pollicis longus (median/AIN) substitutes for the paralysed adductor pollicis (ulnar).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Phalen's test the patient holds the wrists in maximal flexion for 60 seconds; tingling in the median nerve distribution indicates:

options.D: Ulnar nerve entrapment at the elbow

questions.explanation: Phalen's test increases pressure in the carpal tunnel.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Allen's test of the hand assesses:

options.C: Patency of the radial and ulnar arteries

questions.explanation: Delayed flushing of the hand on releasing one artery indicates arterial insufficiency of that vessel.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Bunnell-Littler test, increased PIP flexion when the MCP joint is flexed (intrinsics slackened) indicates tightness of the:
questions.explanation: If PIP flexion improves when the MCP is flexed, the intrinsic muscles are tight; if it stays limited, the PIP capsule is tight.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Bunnell-Littler test, if PIP flexion is restricted regardless of the MCP position, the structure that is tight is the:
questions.explanation: Persistent limitation shows capsular tightness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the tight retinacular ligament test, if DIP flexion increases when the PIP joint is flexed, the structure that is tight is the:
questions.explanation: Relaxing the oblique retinacular ligament by flexing the PIP lets the DIP flex more.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the tight retinacular ligament test, if DIP flexion does NOT increase when the PIP joint is flexed, the structure that is tight is the:
questions.explanation: No improvement with PIP flexion means the DIP capsule limits motion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: FABER (Patrick's) test, with the hip flexed, abducted and externally rotated, is used to detect:

options.D: Hip joint or sacroiliac joint dysfunction

questions.explanation: Pain or a high-lying knee on the tested side suggests hip pathology or iliopsoas spasm.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Thomas test is used to detect:
questions.explanation: When the opposite hip is flexed to the chest, the tested thigh lifting off the table shows hip flexor tightness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Ober's test, the inability of the upper leg to drop toward the table in side-lying indicates tightness of the:
questions.explanation: Ober's test evaluates iliotibial band contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Ely's test (prone, knee passively flexed), spontaneous hip flexion on the tested side indicates tightness of the:
questions.explanation: Ely's test checks rectus femoris length.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the piriformis test the patient lies on the side with the hip flexed to 60 degrees and a downward force is applied at the knee; pain in the buttock indicates:
questions.explanation: Pressure adducts and internally rotates the flexed hip, stretching the piriformis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Craig's test is used to measure:
questions.explanation: In Craig's test the prone knee is flexed to 90 degrees and the hip rotated until the greater trochanter is most prominent; the tibial angle estimates femoral anteversion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Ortolani's and Barlow's tests are used to identify:
questions.explanation: Ortolani reduces a dislocated hip with a clunk; Barlow provokes dislocation of an unstable hip.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The anterior drawer test of the knee, with the knee flexed 90 degrees, tests the:
questions.explanation: Excess anterior tibial translation on the femur means ACL insufficiency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Lachman's test (knee flexed 20-30 degrees, anterior glide of the tibia) tests the:
questions.explanation: Lachman's test is the most sensitive clinical test for ACL rupture.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The posterior drawer test of the knee, with the hip flexed to 45 degrees and the knee to 90 degrees, tests the:
questions.explanation: Excess posterior tibial translation indicates PCL injury.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the posterior sag sign (Godfrey's test) a visible posterior sagging of the tibia indicates injury of the:
questions.explanation: With the hips and knees flexed to 90 degrees, the tibia sags back if the PCL is torn.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A valgus stress test applied at 20-30 degrees of knee flexion tests the:
questions.explanation: Excess valgus movement indicates MCL laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A varus stress test applied at 20-30 degrees of knee flexion tests the:
questions.explanation: Excess varus movement indicates LCL laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Apley's grinding and distraction tests of the knee are used to differentiate:
questions.explanation: Pain on compression with rotation suggests a meniscal lesion; pain on distraction suggests ligament injury.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In McMurray's test, a click or pain on flexing the knee and rotating the tibia externally while extending indicates injury of the:
questions.explanation: External rotation stresses the medial meniscus and internal rotation the lateral meniscus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The patellar tap (ballottement) test indicates:
questions.explanation: The patella 'dances' or floats on a large knee effusion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Clarke's sign (patellar grind test), in which the patient contracts the quadriceps while the patella is pushed down, indicates:
questions.explanation: Pain on quadriceps contraction against patellar compression indicates patellofemoral dysfunction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Noble's compression test, producing pain over the lateral femoral condyle at about 30 degrees of flexion, indicates:
questions.explanation: Noble's test reproduces ITB friction pain at the lateral femoral epicondyle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The patellar apprehension test, in which the patient tries to contract the quadriceps when the patella is pushed laterally, indicates:
questions.explanation: Apprehension shows a history of lateral patellar instability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The mediopatellar plica test is positive when:

options.C: Pain or popping is felt on passive flexion and extension of the knee

questions.explanation: Plica dysfunction produces a palpable band and pain on motion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the anterior drawer test of the ankle, excessive anterior glide of the talus indicates injury of the:
questions.explanation: The anterior drawer test stresses the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The talar tilt test, in which excessive adduction (inversion) of the talus is found, indicates injury of the:
questions.explanation: Inversion talar tilt tests the calcaneofibular ligament; eversion tilt tests the deltoid.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Absence of plantar flexion on squeezing the calf in prone (Thompson's test) indicates:
questions.explanation: The Thompson (Simmonds) test is positive when squeezing the calf fails to plantar flex the foot.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Squeezing the forefoot to compress the metatarsal heads and producing pain (Morton's test) suggests:

options.D: Interdigital (Morton's) neuroma or metatarsal stress fracture

questions.explanation: Morton's test compresses the transverse metatarsal arch.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Spurling's (foraminal compression) test is positive in:
questions.explanation: Reproduction of arm pain with neck extension, side flexion and axial compression indicates cervical radiculopathy.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The vertebral artery (de Kleyn) test, with sustained neck extension and rotation, is used to assess:
questions.explanation: Dizziness, nausea or nystagmus on sustained positions suggest vertebrobasilar compromise.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Hautant's test, in which the arms are held at 90 degrees abduction with eyes closed while the neck is extended and rotated, assesses:
questions.explanation: Loss of arm position suggests vertebral artery compromise rather than a joint problem.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the cervical distraction test, relief of neck and arm symptoms when the neck is passively distracted indicates:

options.D: Nerve root compression at the intervertebral foramen

questions.explanation: Distraction opens the foramina and relieves root compression.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the shoulder abduction (Bakody) relief test, reduction of arm pain when the hand is placed on the head suggests:
questions.explanation: Abducting the arm slackens the nerve root and relieves radicular pain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Lhermitte's sign (shooting pain down the spine on neck flexion) suggests:

options.C: Dural or spinal cord irritation (e.g. multiple sclerosis or cervical myelopathy)

questions.explanation: Neck flexion stretches the cord and produces electric shock-like sensations.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The slump test is used to assess:

options.C: Neurological (neural tension) dysfunction of the lower limb

questions.explanation: Sitting spinal flexion, knee extension and ankle dorsiflexion tension the sciatic nerve and dura.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The straight leg raise (SLR) test mainly tensions the:
questions.explanation: Pain between 30 and 70 degrees suggests a disc lesion irritating the sciatic roots.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The femoral nerve traction (prone knee bend) test reproduces:

options.B: Anterior thigh pain from L2-L4 root irritation
options.D: Posterior thigh pain from L5-S1 irritation

questions.explanation: Prone knee flexion with hip extension stretches the femoral nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The quadrant (extension-rotation) test performed in standing reproduces localised pain in:

options.C: Facet joint dysfunction or foraminal compression

questions.explanation: Extension, side flexion and rotation to one side close the foramen and compress the facet joint.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Stork (one-leg standing) test, in which the patient extends the spine while standing on one leg, is positive for:
questions.explanation: Pain on extension while standing on the ipsilateral leg suggests a pars defect.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Gillet's (PSIS) test, when the patient flexes the hip and knee on the tested side, the PSIS should move:

options.A: Upward in relation to the sacrum
options.B: Downward (inferiorly) in relation to the sacrum

questions.explanation: Failure of the PSIS to drop indicates hypomobility of the sacroiliac joint on that side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Gaenslen's test, extending the hip of the top leg in side-lying with the lower hip flexed reproduces pain from the:
questions.explanation: Gaenslen's test stresses the sacroiliac joint.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In van Gelderen's bicycle test, a patient with lumbar spinal stenosis can cycle for ______ in the slumped (flexed) position than in the upright position.
questions.explanation: Flexion enlarges the canal, so symptoms ease and cycling is tolerated longer; this differentiates stenosis from vascular claudication.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the slump test, adding hip abduction with flexion to 90 degrees places maximum tension on the:
questions.explanation: Hip abduction in the slump test biases the obturator nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A slump test performed in side-lying with the hip extended and knee flexed tensions the:
questions.explanation: The side-lying slump with hip extension and knee flexion is the femoral nerve (prone knee bend) variant.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A modified SLR with hip flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion and foot eversion biases the:
questions.explanation: Dorsiflexion with eversion and toe extension adds tension to the tibial nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A modified SLR with hip flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion and foot inversion biases the:
questions.explanation: Dorsiflexion with inversion adds tension to the sural nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A modified SLR with hip flexion and medial rotation, knee extension, ankle plantar flexion and inversion biases the:
questions.explanation: Plantar flexion with inversion adds tension to the common peroneal nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal carrying angle at the elbow in men is about:
questions.explanation: The carrying angle is about 5 degrees in men and 10-15 degrees in women.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal carrying angle at the elbow in women is about:
questions.explanation: Women have a larger carrying angle because of a wider pelvis and narrower shoulders.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal Q angle in men is about:
questions.explanation: The Q angle is about 13 degrees in men and 18 degrees in women.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal Q angle in women is about:
questions.explanation: A wider pelvis gives women a larger Q angle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Hoover's test, Burn's bench test and Waddell's signs are used to assess:

options.B: Malingering or non-organic low back pain

questions.explanation: These tests identify inconsistent or non-organic behaviour in low back pain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In deep transverse friction massage (DTFM) the massage force is applied ______ to the tissue fibres.

options.A: Along the line of the muscle

questions.explanation: DTFM is applied across (transverse to) the fibre direction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A tendon with a sheath should be placed in a ______ position when DTFM is applied.
questions.explanation: A sheathed tendon is stretched so that the tendon is fixed against the underlying bone while the sheath is rubbed over it; muscle bellies are kept relaxed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: After DTFM to a muscle, ______ movement should be encouraged.
questions.explanation: Gentle active movement maintains the mobility of the freed fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Maitland's grading, grade I oscillations are:

options.A: Small amplitude at the beginning of range
options.B: Large amplitude to the end of range
options.D: Small amplitude at the end of range

questions.explanation: Grade I: small amplitude at the start of the range, used for pain relief.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Maitland's grading, grade II oscillations are:

options.A: Large amplitude within the range (not reaching the limit)
options.B: Small amplitude at the beginning of range

questions.explanation: Grade II: large-amplitude oscillations in the free part of the range.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Maitland's grading, grade III oscillations are:

options.A: Small amplitude at the beginning of range
options.B: Large amplitude up to the end of the range

questions.explanation: Grade III: large amplitude oscillations into resistance, used to stretch.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Maitland's grading, grade IV oscillations are:

options.A: Small amplitude at the beginning of range
options.C: Small amplitude at the end of range
options.D: Large amplitude at the end of range

questions.explanation: Grade IV: small-amplitude oscillations at the limit of range to stretch tight tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Grade V in Maitland's mobilisation refers to a:

options.A: Low amplitude high velocity thrust at the end of range
options.C: Small amplitude at the start of range

questions.explanation: Grade V is a manipulation (thrust).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: To reduce pain and muscle spasm, Maitland grades ______ are used.
questions.explanation: Grades I and II (non-stretching) are used for pain; III and IV for stiffness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: To stretch shortened muscles or tight capsules and ligaments, Maitland grades ______ are used.
questions.explanation: Grades III and IV take the tissues to resistance and into stretch.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's traction/glide grading, grade I (a traction force of small amplitude) is used to:
questions.explanation: Grade I (loosen) neutralises joint pressure to relieve pain; II takes up slack; III stretches.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade III glide is used to:
questions.explanation: Grade III applies a stretch force to tighten the joint capsule and surrounding tissues.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In Kaltenborn's grading, grade II is the force used to:
questions.explanation: Grade II (take up slack) tightens the tissue without stretching it.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A thrust manipulation is performed when the patient reaches the:
questions.explanation: The thrust is applied at the end of exhalation when muscle relaxation is greatest.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of McKenzie's postural syndrome?

options.A: No pain with activity or movement

questions.explanation: Postural syndrome involves intermittent pain from sustained positions with no deformity and no radicular signs.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of McKenzie's derangement syndrome?

options.A: No pain with activity or movement

questions.explanation: In derangement, pain is related to movement and posture, with directional preference and possible loss of movement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of McKenzie's dysfunction syndrome?

options.C: Symptoms disappear when loading is removed

questions.explanation: Dysfunction is caused by adaptive shortening with local pain at end range and no peripheral symptoms.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Movement of pain from the buttocks or legs toward the centre of the back during exercises is called:
questions.explanation: Centralisation is a good prognostic sign in McKenzie's derangement syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Movement of pain from the back to the buttocks or legs with activity or exercise is called:
questions.explanation: Peripheralisation indicates the wrong direction of movement or worsening derangement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement is FALSE for centralisation?

options.C: The risk of damage is high

questions.explanation: Centralisation is a favourable response with a low risk of harm.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which statement is FALSE for peripheralisation?

options.B: The risk of damage is low
options.C: Pain moves from the centre to the periphery
options.D: It calls for stopping the provoking exercise

questions.explanation: Peripheralisation carries a risk of worsening and should prompt a change of direction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For the dysfunction syndrome McKenzie advocated:

options.C: Repetitive movement in the direction of the dysfunction to remodel tissue

questions.explanation: Dysfunction is treated by repeated end-range loading into the restricted direction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Centralisation of pain is seen in:
questions.explanation: Centralisation occurs with directional preference movements in derangement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For asymmetrical pain with a lateral shift (listing) in a scoliotic patient, McKenzie's first treatment is:
questions.explanation: In McKenzie's approach the lateral shift must be corrected before extension-based exercises.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Grade 0 on the peripheral pulse scale means:
questions.explanation: 0 absent, 1+ diminished, 2+ normal, 3+ full, 4+ bounding.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Grade 1+ on the peripheral pulse scale means:
questions.explanation: 1+ is a weak or diminished pulse.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Grade 2+ on the peripheral pulse scale means:
questions.explanation: 2+ is the normal pulse.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Grade 3+ on the peripheral pulse scale means:
questions.explanation: 3+ is a full, increased pulse.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Grade 4+ on the peripheral pulse scale means:
questions.explanation: 4+ is a strong bounding pulse that is easily seen.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The aortic valve area is located at the:

options.A: 2nd intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.B: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line
options.C: 2nd intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.D: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border

questions.explanation: The aortic area is the right second intercostal space.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The pulmonary valve area is located at the:

options.A: 2nd intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.C: 2nd intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.D: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line

questions.explanation: The pulmonary area is the left second intercostal space.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The tricuspid valve area is located at the:

options.A: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: 2nd intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: 2nd intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.D: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line

questions.explanation: The tricuspid area is the lower left sternal border.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The mitral valve area (apex) is located at the:

options.A: 2nd intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: 4th intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.C: 2nd intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.D: 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line on the left

questions.explanation: The mitral area is at the cardiac apex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The first heart sound (S1, 'lub') is associated with closure of the:
questions.explanation: S1 marks the start of ventricular systole when the mitral and tricuspid valves close.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The second heart sound (S2, 'dub') is associated with closure of the:
questions.explanation: S2 marks the end of systole and the start of diastole.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The first heart sound is decreased in:
questions.explanation: A long PR interval lets the AV valves float partly shut, softening S1.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The second heart sound is decreased in:
questions.explanation: A stiff, calcified aortic valve reduces the aortic component of S2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A systolic murmur occurs:

options.B: Between S2 and the next S1

questions.explanation: Systole lies between the first and second heart sounds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A diastolic murmur occurs:

options.A: Between S2 and the next S1

questions.explanation: Diastole is between the second and first sounds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The third heart sound (S3) is heard:
questions.explanation: S3 is a ventricular gallop from rapid filling, seen in heart failure.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The fourth heart sound (S4) is heard:
questions.explanation: S4 is an atrial gallop heard late in diastole before the first heart sound.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Normal capillary refill time (return of colour after release of pressure) is:
questions.explanation: Capillary refill above 2 seconds suggests poor peripheral perfusion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Homans' sign (pain in the calf on passive dorsiflexion) is positive in:
questions.explanation: Calf pain on dorsiflexion suggests DVT, though the sign is not reliable.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A positive Stemmer's sign (inability to pinch the skin at the base of the second toe or finger) is seen in:
questions.explanation: Thickened skin that cannot be pinched is characteristic of lymphoedema.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Claudication pain that is unbearable and excruciating is graded as:
questions.explanation: On the 4-point scale: 1 minimal, 2 moderate, 3 intense, 4 excruciating.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Claudication pain that is intense and the person cannot take his attention from it is graded as:
questions.explanation: Grade 3 is intense pain that cannot be ignored.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the person's attention can be diverted from the claudication pain, it is graded as:
questions.explanation: Grade 2 is moderate pain that distraction relieves.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Mild but definite claudication pain of modest level is graded as:
questions.explanation: Grade 1 is minimal, definite discomfort.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal respiratory rate in adults is:
questions.explanation: Normal adult respiratory rate is 12-20 breaths per minute.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A pattern of reduced rate and depth of breathing with periods of apnoea in between is:
questions.explanation: Cheyne-Stokes shows waxing and waning of breath depth with apnoea; it is seen in heart failure and brain injury.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In metabolic acidosis the rate and depth of breathing are increased. This pattern is known as:
questions.explanation: Kussmaul breathing is deep, rapid 'air hunger' breathing in diabetic ketoacidosis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With medullary damage, breathing becomes irregular with periods of apnoea in between. This pattern is known as:
questions.explanation: Biot's (ataxic) breathing indicates medullary injury.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal inspiratory to expiratory (I:E) ratio at rest is:
questions.explanation: Expiration is normally about twice as long as inspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With activity the I:E ratio in normal individuals becomes:
questions.explanation: During exercise inspiratory and expiratory times become almost equal.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Individuals with COPD typically have an I:E ratio of:
questions.explanation: Air trapping prolongs expiration in COPD.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: People with COPD (upper chest breathers) typically show a:
questions.explanation: Hyperinflation increases the anteroposterior diameter, giving a barrel chest.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In pectus carinatum (pigeon chest) the sternum:
questions.explanation: Pectus carinatum is anterior protrusion of the sternum.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In pectus excavatum (funnel chest), the following is true EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: In funnel chest the sternum is depressed, not elevated.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which normal breath sound is heard over the trachea and main stem bronchi?
questions.explanation: Bronchial breath sounds are loud, high-pitched with a longer expiratory phase.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which normal breath sound is heard all over the chest but not over the trachea and main stem bronchi?
questions.explanation: Vesicular sounds are soft and low-pitched with inspiration longer than expiration.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which normal breath sound is heard in the supraclavicular and suprascapular regions?
questions.explanation: Bronchovesicular sounds are heard over the main bronchi near the sternum and between the scapulae.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which are the soft, low-pitched normal breath sounds heard for longer during inspiration than expiration?
questions.explanation: Vesicular sounds have an inspiratory phase about three times longer than the expiratory phase.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which are the tubular, high-pitched normal breath sounds heard equally during inspiration and expiration with a pause between the two?
questions.explanation: Bronchial sounds are heard over the trachea; elsewhere they imply consolidation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which are soft normal breath sounds heard equally during inspiration and expiration without a pause between the two?
questions.explanation: Bronchovesicular sounds are intermediate in pitch and intensity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the presence of secretions, discontinuous abnormal breath sounds heard mainly during inspiration are:
questions.explanation: Crackles are discontinuous bubbling sounds from airway secretions or reopening of airways.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Abnormal continuous breath sounds heard mainly during expiration because of bronchospasm are:
questions.explanation: Wheezes are musical, continuous sounds from narrowed airways.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Absence of breath sounds over a lung zone is typically seen in:
questions.explanation: Air in the pleural space (or lung collapse) prevents sound transmission.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A high-pitched wheeze that is continuous in nature and heard during both inspiration and expiration is called ______ and suggests ______.
questions.explanation: Stridor indicates a narrowed upper airway, such as the larynx or trachea.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On percussion, a tympanic (hyper-resonant) note is heard in:
questions.explanation: Air in the pleural space gives a hyper-resonant percussion note.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal FEV1/FVC ratio (in %) in healthy subjects is about:
questions.explanation: Normal FEV1/FVC is about 75-85 percent.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following FEV1/FVC values suggests a restrictive condition?
questions.explanation: In restrictive disease FEV1/FVC is normal or high because FVC falls proportionally more.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following FEV1/FVC values suggests an obstructive condition?
questions.explanation: A low FEV1/FVC (below 70 percent) indicates airflow obstruction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: FEV1/FVC is normal or high in ______ conditions because there is a greater reduction in FVC.
questions.explanation: FVC is reduced more than FEV1 in restrictive disease.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: FEV1/FVC is low in ______ conditions because FVC is reduced less than FEV1.
questions.explanation: In obstruction, FEV1 falls much more than FVC.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a restrictive condition, total lung capacity (TLC) is:
questions.explanation: Restriction reduces lung expansion and TLC.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In an obstructive condition, residual volume (RV) is:
questions.explanation: Air trapping increases residual volume in COPD.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a restrictive condition, residual volume (RV) is:
questions.explanation: Lung volumes are all smaller in restrictive disease.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In order to assess the severity of an obstructive condition, which of the following is considered?
questions.explanation: FEV1 percent predicted grades the severity of obstruction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In order to assess the severity of a restrictive condition, which of the following is considered?
questions.explanation: TLC percent predicted grades the severity of restriction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A low FEV1/FVC together with a low TLC means the condition is:
questions.explanation: Both obstruction and restriction coexist.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: FRC and TLC ______ in obstructive conditions.
questions.explanation: Hyperinflation and air trapping raise lung volumes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: FRC and TLC ______ in restrictive conditions.
questions.explanation: Restriction reduces all lung volumes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be measured by simple spirometry?
questions.explanation: Residual volume cannot be exhaled, so it needs helium dilution or body plethysmography.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Coving (scooping) of the expiratory limb of the flow-volume loop is seen in ______ conditions.
questions.explanation: Airflow limitation causes concave expiratory curves in COPD and asthma.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The inspiratory limb of the flow-volume loop is normal or only slightly reduced in ______ condition.
questions.explanation: Obstructive disease mainly affects expiratory flow.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Coving of the expiratory limb is NOT seen in:
questions.explanation: In restrictive disease the loop is a small but normally shaped version of the normal loop.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Flattening of both the inspiratory and expiratory limbs of the flow-volume loop is seen in:
questions.explanation: A fixed large-airway lesion limits flow equally in both phases.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: FEF 25-75% is an indicator of:
questions.explanation: FEF25-75 reflects mid-expiratory flow through small airways.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) is an indicator of:
questions.explanation: PEFR depends on effort and large airway calibre.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: To assess bronchodilator reversibility, the primary index used is:
questions.explanation: The change in FEV1 after a bronchodilator is used to grade reversibility.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A change of less than 5 percent in FEV1 after a bronchodilator is considered:
questions.explanation: Less than 5 percent change is not significant.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
